goal: Reduce latency for one complete offline batch=32 image inference, preserving the source quality checks.
completion: One measured invocation is exactly one infer(model, pixels) call (resnet_inference.py:15-16): model(pixel_values=pixels).logits under torch.inference_mode() on the pretrained FP32 ResNet-18, with pixels the pre-built GPU-resident contiguous 32x3x224x224 float32 NCHW batch (images[torch.arange(32, device='cuda') % 3], resnet_inference.py:29). The completion boundary is the torch.cuda.synchronize() after the forward (resnet_inference.py:42-47), which the framework's post-run CUDA synchronization supplies, so adapter.run() performs only the forward pass. Excluded from the measured invocation: model loading, host-to-device input transfer, batch construction, reference/actual pair construction, close_check/negative_check and the exact top-1 assert, warmup calls, the 5-repeat timing loop with reset_peak_memory_stats, summarize/save of result.json, and optional --profile diagnostics (common.py:87-105).
state_protocol: prepare(context, request) applies the source configure() policy (4 CPU threads, 1 interop thread, manual_seed 20261020, TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark=False, float32_matmul_precision('highest')) with the worker-bound context['device'], loads ResNetForImageClassification from request['assets']['assets_dir'] with local_files_only=True and dtype=torch.float32 onto that device in eval mode, loads pixels.npy onto the device, and builds the frozen batch=32 input by indexing with torch.arange(32, device=device) % len(images) followed by .contiguous(); state keeps model, the full images fixture tensor (kept live exactly as the source holds it at its timer), the pixels batch, batch size and parameter count. reset(state) is a no-op: inference is stateless, eval weights are immutable, and run() creates its output inside a fresh request-local torch.inference_mode() context; the source resets nothing between timed calls, and the process group (none here) is never destroyed. run(state) executes the entire frozen workload, one forward returning the full [32, 1000] logits tensor. observe(state, result) returns detached CPU copies of the complete logits and the argmax class-id integers. metrics(state, result, elapsed_ms) derives latency_ms from elapsed_ms, images_per_second from batch 32 and elapsed_ms, and queries torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() outside the timer. models(state) exposes {'model': model} for discovery and controlled replacement.
invariants: Numerical policy frozen from common.py:34-42: torch.float32 weights and inputs, torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'), torch.set_num_threads(4), torch.set_num_interop_threads(1), torch.manual_seed(20261020).

Batch semantics frozen: batch=32 formed by cycling the 3 preprocessed fixture images in pixels.npy via images[torch.arange(32, device=device) % 3].contiguous(); FP32 NCHW, GPU-resident before timing; the host-to-device transfer happens once in prepare, outside the timed region.

Model frozen: microsoft/resnet-18 revision 65a5785d9156231087c481e0c7dd33a5ff6f7e3e pinned by asset-manifest.json, loaded with local_files_only=True and dtype=torch.float32, moved to context['device'], eval mode; no architecture, precision or weight changes.
Every measured call runs under torch.inference_mode() exactly as the source's @torch.inference_mode() decorator on infer (resnet_inference.py:14-16).

Correctness observations are the full 1000-class logits for all 32 rows plus the argmax top-1 class ids; logits are compared with atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4 and top-1 labels exactly (require_exact_top1); the negative control must reject a +1 corruption of the reference (common.py:79-84). These checks are framework quality infrastructure, not part of run().

The objective latency_ms is the source's per-sample end-to-end wall time of one complete forward (time.perf_counter_ns across infer plus trailing torch.cuda.synchronize, resnet_inference.py:42-47); it must not be renamed to a cached-only or throughput metric, and the source attaches no constraints to latency goals.

images_per_second = batch * 1e9 / elapsed_ns and peak_allocated_bytes = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() are recorded per sample as in resnet_inference.py:48; they belong to the row's other goals and are not imported as latency constraints.
Single-GPU single-process workload: no process group, no NCCL, no communication; model, images and pixels all live on context['device'], never on a self-chosen physical GPU.

The timed region contains only the forward pass; model loading, input transfer, reference construction, correctness checks, warmup (2) and the 5-repeat statistics loop remain outside run(), and the framework's boundary synchronizations are not duplicated inside run().
The full images fixture tensor (3x3x224x224) stays referenced in state during timing, matching the source's live Python references at its timer so the memory footprint is preserved.
No downloads: all weights, config and data come from request['assets'] at their pinned absolute paths.
assumptions: adapter.run() repeats exactly one infer() call on the fixed GPU batch; the framework's warmup=2/repeats=5 looping, reset of CUDA peak stats immediately before its timer, and CUDA synchronization at both boundaries reproduce the source timing loop (common.py defaults, resnet_inference.py:38-49).

reset() is intentionally a no-op because the workload is stateless inference: the source performs no per-call clearing or caching inside its timed invocation, and run() creates request-local state under a fresh inference_mode context.

observe() returns detached CPU copies of the full logits tensor and integer predicted class ids; the reference/actual pair construction, close_check, negative_check and the exact top-1 assert are benchmark/quality infrastructure handled by the framework around the adapter.

metrics() exposes the frozen objective latency_ms derived from elapsed_ms, plus the source's per-sample project metrics images_per_second (from the unchanged work amount batch=32) and peak_allocated_bytes (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() queried outside the timer), and the static parameter_count (11689512); no profiler or timing is run inside run()/metrics().

from_pretrained is pointed at request['assets']['assets_dir'] exactly as the source used --assets, with dtype=torch.float32 as in transformers 5.x usage in the source; pixels.npy supplies the 3 preprocessed fixture images (verified shape (3, 3, 224, 224) float32).

set_mode/before_run are omitted: the source has no separate correctness-capture path (infer always returns full logits), no source-defined coordination is needed for this single-process workload, and the single forward has no meaningful subphases to annotate.
The held-out workload unseen_batch (batch=7) and the other suites in workloads.json (qwen_inference, gpt2_ddp_training) are not part of this frozen request and are not implemented by the adapter.
Required_observations is empty and distributed_backend is null, so no communication collector fields are expected; latency is ordinary end-to-end per-call time.
